name: Calendly
appType: OAuth app (OAuth 2.1, PKCE), Sandbox or Production
summary: No review gate: a Production OAuth app works for any Calendly user the moment you create it. Two gotchas: each app takes exactly one redirect URI, and new apps get no API access until you pick scopes.

composio.note: Composio's managed app lets users connect today. Bring your own for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes or your own rate limits.

steps.title: Create a Calendly developer account
steps.detail: Sign up on developer.calendly.com with GitHub or Google. It is **separate from your Calendly user account**.

steps.title: Create a Sandbox app for development
steps.detail: OAuth apps → Create OAuth app → Environment: Sandbox. Sandbox allows `http://localhost` redirect URIs.
steps.agent: Pick the minimal scopes and wire up PKCE locally

steps.title: Choose scopes up front
steps.detail: New apps get **no API access** until scopes are selected. Request the minimum; adding scopes later means users must re-authorize.
steps.agent: Map each agent feature to the scope catalog

steps.title: Create a separate Production app
steps.detail: Production requires https and accepts **exactly one redirect URI**, so use one app for Composio BYO (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) and another for your own callback.
steps.human: Create them and store the secrets

steps.title: Handle tokens the Calendly way
steps.detail: Access tokens last 2 hours; refresh tokens don't expire until used (store the new one every time); max 8 token requests per user per minute.
steps.agent: Implement refresh with single-use refresh tokens and backoff

launchToday: Or create your Production app today: there is no approval queue.
rejections: No review exists, so failures show up at runtime: redirect_uri mismatch (one URI per app)
403 missing scope: the app was created without the scope the endpoint needs

blockers.fix: The token lacks a scope. Add it to the app and send the user through OAuth again.
Refresh tokens are single-use. Persist the new refresh token from every refresh response.
Production apps take one redirect URI. Create a second app.

uncertain: Calendly's docs describe no review gate for Production apps. That is confirmed by its absence, not by an explicit statement.
Whether webhook delivery depends on the end user's Calendly plan isn't stated on the pages read.
